subject: Urgent: Sparkline production latency & errors — network path investigation
messages:
From: Tim Ellis <tim.ellis@sparkline.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-21T08:12:00Z
Subject: Intermittent 5xxs and latency spikes - Sparkline Retail

Ben —

We're seeing a production-wide increase in 5xxs and request tail latency starting around 07:50 UTC. Error rate peaked ~6.2% for token-generation requests and mean P95 latency jumped from ~120ms -> 1.2s. Impacting checkout personalization, multiple customers reporting timeouts.

We've attached a short packet capture and a brief log sample (sparkline_edge_trace.pcap). Key notes:
- Errors correlate with retries and a cluster of timeouts to redwood-edge-us-east-1:443
- DNS lookups for infgw.sparkline.net are bouncing between two resolvers for several seconds
- Observed increased SYN retransmits and occasional RSTs from an inline proxy cluster

Can you confirm if there are known routing changes, peering degradations, or firewall/proxy throttles on your side? This is P1 for us.

Thanks,
Tim
Director of Platform Ops
Sparkline Retail

Attachments: sparkline_edge_trace.pcap
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Ellis <tim.ellis@sparkline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-21T08:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xxs and latency spikes - Sparkline Retail

Tim —

Thanks for the signal and the capture. I'm looking at this now and have looped in Marissa (customer lead) to coordinate. Initial ask: can you confirm the client region and any recent infra changes on your side (WAF rules, proxy config)? I'm going to escalate internally for immediate path isolation and a short-term mitigation while SRE investigates.

Immediate actions I'm proposing:
- Flip traffic to our secondary peering point for Sparkline (if ok with you) to see if errors abate
- Temporarily reduce client-side parallelism for token requests (workaround)
- Share timestamped pcap and samples with SRE for traceroute correlation

I'll follow up in 10–15 with internal owners.

—Ben
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

What we know so far:
- Errors appear to align with traffic hitting our us-east egress/peering cluster
- Customer traces show DNS flapping and RSTs from an inline proxy
- Customer requests verification of any recent firewall/proxy/peering changes on our side

Request / ask list (prioritized):
1) Grace: quick validation of peering health (BGP anomalies, intermediate NAT exhaustion), and capture of our edge-facing proxy metrics for last hour.
2) Vivek: exec decision on fallback to Reserved/Dedicated route or cross-region redirect for Sparkline (customer will accept short traffic shift if it reduces errors). Also advise on SLA/credits if we confirm service degradation.
3) Marissa: keep customer calm — coordinate the permission to shift to alternate peering and confirm timing window.

I've attached the customer pcap and will append internal traces after I get them. This is P1; please mark urgent.

—Ben

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-21T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: [ACTION REQUIRED] Sparkline P1 - production latency + 5xx spike (need exec/SRE attention)

Team —

Quick update from SRE investigation (first 30m):
- BGP/peering plane: no widespread BGP withdraws or route flaps visible from our control plane. Peering sessions show normal uptime.
- Proxy cluster: metrics show CPU and socket backlog spikes on proxy-pool-us-east-1-a coincident with the customer's error window. There are increased accept queue drops and rising RSTs.
- DNS: customer-visible DNS TTLs were stable, but our edge resolver cluster saw high error rates to one upstream resolver for ~90s; we observed cached negative responses which map to the customer's lookup failures.

Initial hypothesis: a cascade where an upstream resolver transient issue caused a burst of retry/parallel requests into the same proxy worker set, which in turn hit socket limits and produced RSTs + 502/504s.

Immediate remediation applied (09:00 UTC):
- Enabled per-customer connection limiting on edge proxies for Sparkline to smooth bursts (temporary guardrail).
- Programmatically shifted 30% of Sparkline traffic to us-east-2 peering (controlled diversion).
- Flushed cache entries for affected DNS names on our edge resolver cluster.

Impact so far: error rate dropped from 6.2% -> 0.9% within 6 minutes of mitigations. P95 latency returned to ~160ms.

Next steps (SRE):
- Continue 15m monitoring window; collect full tcpdump and application logs (attaching runbook + traces).
- Postmortem to include: proxy socket tuning, resolver upstream retries, and whether we should add an automatic resolver-failover rule for edge clusters.

Attachments: redwood_path_runbook_v2.pdf, sparkline_edge_trace.pcap

—Grace
Sr. SRE, Edge Reliability
Redwood Inference

Tim —

Short update and resolution summary: thanks for the quick triage on your side. Our SRE team identified a transient resolver failure upstream that amplified retry traffic into a subset of our edge proxy workers; those workers experienced socket backlog exhaustion and produced RSTs, causing 502/504s and latency spikes.

Actions taken (summary):
- 09:00 UTC: edge per-customer connection limiting enabled to smooth bursts
- 09:00–09:30 UTC: controlled diversion of 30% traffic to us-east-2 peering; error rate quickly dropped
- 09:06 UTC onward: DNS cache flush and upstream resolver failover rules applied

Current state: error rate now <1%, P95 latency ~160ms, monitoring in extended window. We'll keep the diversion in place while we complete a deeper postmortem and implement longer-term mitigations (proxy socket tuning, automatic resolver failover).

Marissa will coordinate any commercial follow-up; we will review the incident against SLA and propose credits if applicable. We'll schedule a 1-hour postmortem this week and share notes.

If you can, please confirm whether your teams saw any residual errors after 11:00 UTC so we have symmetric observability.

Appreciate the patience — we'll follow up with a formal incident report.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
